question: A Ltd is following Ind AS for the first time for the year ended 31st March, 20X4. What all period balance sheet to be covered in its first Ind AS financial statements? Answer:
options: (a) 1st April 20X2
(b) 31st March 20X3
(c) 31st March 20X4
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: Company XYZ Pvt Ltd was having its net worth of ₹ 230 Crores as on 31st March 2020. It made a profit of ₹ 30 Crores in FY 20-21 and made a loss of ₹ 15 crores in FY 21-22. From which date it is required to apply Ind AS? Answer:
options: (a) Accounting periods beginning on or after 1st April 2020
(b) Accounting periods beginning on or after 1st April 2021
(c) Accounting periods beginning on or after 1st April 2022
(d) It is not required to comply with Ind AS as its Net worth as on 31st March 2022 is below ₹ 250 Cr.
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (b) Accounting periods beginning on or after 1st April 2021

question: Ind AS 103 contains additional guidance on common control transaction which is not there in IFRS 3. How this can be termed? Answer:
options: (a) Carve in
(b) Carve out
(c) Exception
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (a) Carve in

question: Which one of the following is the benefit of implementation of Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) in India? Answer:
options: (a) Increase in net profitability
(b) Minimised disclosure requirements
(c) Access to domestic capital market
(d) Global harmonization helps grow FII and FDI interests
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (d) Global harmonization helps grow FII and FDI interests

question: For preparing Ind AS based financial statements with transition date 1st April, 20X5, what all guidance needs to be referred by A Ltd.? Answer:
options: (a) Ind AS 1
(b) Division II of Schedule III to the Companies Act, 2013
(c) Guidance Note on preparation and presentation of Ind AS based financial statements issued by ICAI
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: Country X has taken approach of implementing Global Accounting Standards in its country with some significant changes in line with their national economic policies. This would be termed as Answer:
options: (a) Adoption of Global Accounting Standards
(b) Convergence with Global Accounting standards
(c) Adoption of Global Accounting standards with limitations
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (b) Convergence with Global Accounting standards

question: Company ABC Insurance Pvt Ltd is engaged in the business of insurance and is having a net worth of ₹ 1,000 crores as on 31st March 2017. From which financial year it is required to apply Ind AS? Answer:
options: (d) Yet not required to apply Ind AS
explanation: [CHAPTER 1 - Introduction to Indian Accounting Standards] Correct Option: (d) Yet not required to apply Ind AS

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to Reporting Period? Answer:
options: (a) Financial statements are prepared for a specified period of time
(b) It helps users of financial statements to identify and assess changes and trends
(c) Financial statements provide comparative information for at least one preceding reporting period
(d) Financial statements should not provide comparative information for more than one preceding reporting periods
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (d) Financial statements should not provide comparative information for more than one preceding reporting periods

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to CONTROL? An entity controls an economic resource if: Answer:
options: (a) it has the present ability to direct the use of the economic resource
(b) it obtains the economic benefits that may flow from it
(c) if one party controls an economic resource, other party may also control that resource
(d) Control of an economic resource usually arises from an ability to enforce legal rights
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (c) if one party controls an economic resource, other party may also control that resource

question: The usefulness of financial information is enhanced if it is: Answer:
options: (a) comparable, verifiable, perfect and understandable
(b) comparable, verifiable, timely and objective
(c) effective, verifiable, timely and understandable
(d) comparable, verifiable, timely and understandable
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (d) comparable, verifiable, timely and understandable

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE for Consolidated and unconsolidated financial statements? Answer:
options: (a) Consolidated financial statements provide information of both the parent and its subsidiaries as a single reporting entity
(b) Unconsolidated financial statements are designed to provide parents information and not about those of its subsidiaries
(c) Consolidated financial statements are designed to provide separate information of any particular subsidiary
(d) A parent may require / choose, to prepare unconsolidated financial statements in addition to consolidated financial statements
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (c) Consolidated financial statements are designed to provide separate information of any particular subsidiary

question: Which of the following statements are TRUE with respect to The Reporting Entity? Answer:
options: (a) A reporting entity has to be a single entity only and it cannot comprise more than one entity
(b) A reporting entity is an entity that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements
(c) If a reporting entity is the parent alone, the reporting entitys financial statements are referred to as consolidated financial statements
(d) If two or more entities are all linked by a parent-subsidiary relationship, they are referred to as combined financial statements
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (b) A reporting entity is an entity that is required, or chooses, to prepare financial statements

question: Which of the following definitions is incorrect? Answer:
options: (a) An Asset is a present economic resource controlled by the entity as a result of past events
(b) A Liability is a past obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result of present events
(c) An Equity is the residual interest in the assets of the entity after deducting all its liabilities
(d) Income is the increases in assets, or decreases in liabilities, that result in increases in equity, other than those relating to contributions from holders of equity claims
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (b) A Liability is a past obligation of the entity to transfer an economic resource as a result of present events

question: To be a perfectly faithful representation, a depiction would not have the following characteristic: Answer:
options: (a) Complete
(b) Unintentional error is allowed
(c) Neutral
(d) Free from error
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (b) Unintentional error is allowed

question: Which of the following is true with respect to the cost constraint on useful financial information? Answer:
options: (a) Cost is a pervasive constraint on the information that can be provided by financial reporting
(b) IASB considers costs and benefits in individual reporting entities only
(c) For application of cost constraint, no assessment of benefits of reporting is done
(d) Users do not incur any costs in reporting and analysing financial information
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (a) Cost is a pervasive constraint on the information that can be provided by financial reporting

question: Which of the following is not the limitation of 'General Purpose Financial Reporting'? Answer:
options: (a) It cannot provide all of the information that existing and potential investors need
(b) The users of reports need to consider pertinent information from other sources
(c) Information given in financial statements help to estimate the value of the reporting entity
(d) Reports are not primarily directed to other parties, such as regulators and lenders etc. Chapter 2 Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian Accounting Standards (Ind AS) 5
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (c) Information given in financial statements help to estimate the value of the reporting entity

question: Which of the following statements is FALSE with respect to Going concern assumption? Answer:
options: (a) There is fundamental assumption that the reporting entity is a going concern
(b) Reporting entity will continue in operation for the foreseeable future
(c) There is no need to describe the basis used in financial statements, if the entity has the intention of liquidation
(d) In case of liquidation, financial statements may have to be prepared on a different basis
explanation: [CHAPTER 2 - Conceptual Framework for Financial Reporting under Indian] Correct Option: (c) There is no need to describe the basis used in financial statements, if the entity has the intention of liquidation

question: An entity whose financial statements comply with Ind AS shall make an _________ statement of such compliance in the notes Answer:
options: (a) Explicit and reserved
(b) Implicit and unreserved
(c) Explicit and unreserved
(d) Implicit and reserved
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (c) Explicit and unreserved

question: Application of Ind AS 1 is important for: Answer:
options: (a) Preparation of general-purpose financial statements
(b) Presentation of general-purpose financial statements
(c) Preparation and presentation of general-purpose financial statements
(d) Preparation, presentation and disclosure in the general-purpose financial statements
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (c) Preparation and presentation of general-purpose financial statements

question: Which of the following information of the entity is not mandatory to be displayed prominently, and is to be repeated when necessary for the information presented to be understandable? Answer:
options: (a) Name of the reporting entity or other means of identification, and any change in that information from the end of the preceding reporting period
(b) Whether the financial statements cover the individual entity or a group of entities
(c) Equity pattern showing the Names of major shareholdings in the entity
(d) Level of rounding used in presenting amounts in the financial statements
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (c) Equity pattern showing the Names of major shareholdings in the entity

question: An inappropriate accounting policy of the entity cannot be rectified by the following ways: Answer:
options: (a) Disclosure of the accounting policies used
(b) By notes
(c) Explanatory material
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: An entity presents an analysis of expenses recognised in the profit or loss using a classification based on the nature of expenses method. Which of the following is not the classification using the nature of expense? Answer:
options: (a) Employee benefits expense
(b) Selling and distribution expenses
(c) Amortisation expense
(d) Depreciation expense
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (b) Selling and distribution expenses

question: Ind AS 1 applies to all entities except: Answer:
options: (a) Those that present consolidated financial statements
(b) Those present separate financial statements
(c) Both of the above
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (d) None of the above

question: An entity shall present a third balance sheet as at the beginning of the preceding period in addition to the minimum comparative financial statements if: Answer:
options: (a) It applies an accounting policy retrospectively
(b) If there is change in accounting estimates
(c) Correction of previous year error
(d) Both (a) and (c) above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (a) It applies an accounting policy retrospectively

question: As per Ind AS 1, the amount in the other comprehensive income will __________ Answer:
options: (a) Not be reclassified subsequently to profit or loss
(b) Be reclassified subsequently to profit or loss when specific conditions are met
(c) Both (a) and (b)
(d) Directly recognised in equity always
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 1 “Presentation of Financial Statements”] Correct Option: (c) Both (a) and (b)

question: Income tax expense should be accrued using the best estimate of the weighted average annual income tax rate expected for the __________ Answer:
options: (a) Interim period
(b) Year to date period
(c) Full financial year
(d) Current period and comparative period
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (c) Full financial year

question: An entity may reverse an impairment loss recognized in a previous interim period in respect of goodwill in the subsequent period. Answer:
options: (a) TRUE
(b) FALSE
(c) Partially True
(d) Partially False
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (b) FALSE

question: The standard defines Interim Financial Report as a financial report for an interim period that contains a set of __________ financial statements. Answer:
options: (a) Complete
(b) Condensed
(c) Financial statement similar to annual
(d) Complete or condensed
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (d) Complete or condensed

question: Which of the following events and transaction is not mandatorily required to disclose in Interim financial statements in accordance with Ind AS 34? Answer:
options: (a) The reversal of any provisions for the costs of restructuring
(b) The assumptions used in the actuarial valuation of defined benefit plan
(c) Acquisitions and disposals of items of property, plant and equipment
(d) Litigation settlements
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (b) The assumptions used in the actuarial valuation of defined benefit plan

question: Which of the following is not the minimum components of an interim financial report? Answer:
options: (a) Condensed balance sheet
(b) Condensed statement of changes in equity
(c) Condensed statement of cash flows
(d) Comparative information in respect of the preceding period
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (d) Comparative information in respect of the preceding period

question: According to Ind AS 34, interim period is a financial reporting period Answer:
options: (a) Shorter than 12 months
(b) Shorter than a full financial year
(c) Of 3 months
(d) Of 6 months
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (b) Shorter than a full financial year

question: An entity is not required to present basic and diluted earnings per share as the components of profit or loss for an interim period. Answer:
options: (a) TRUE
(b) FALSE
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (b) FALSE

question: Ind AS 34 mandates the following in relation to interim financial reports Answer:
options: (a) Which entities should publish interim financial reports
(b) How frequently it should publish
(c) How soon it should publish after the end of interim period
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (d) None of the above

question: An entity prepares quarterly interim financial reports in accordance with AS 25. The entity is engaged in sale of mobile phones and normally 5% of customers claim on their warranty. The provision in the first quarter was calculated as 5% of sales to date, which was ₹ 10 million. However, in the second quarter, a fault was found and warranty claims were expected to be 10% for the whole of the year. Sales in the second quarter were ₹ 15 million. What would be the provision charged in the second quarters interim financial statements? Answer:
options: (a) ₹ 1 million
(b) ₹ 2 million
(c) ₹ 1.25 million
(d) ₹ 1.5 million
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 2 million

question: If an entity publishes a set of condensed financial statements in its interim financial report, those condensed statements shall include, at a minimum, each of the headings and subtotals that were included in its most recent annual financial statements and the selected explanatory notes as required by this Standard. Answer:
options: (a) TRUE
(b) FALSE
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 34 “Interim Financial Reporting”] Correct Option: (a) TRUE

question: As per Ind AS 7, for non-financial entities in the statement of cashflows, interest paid and interest and dividend received is classified as Answer:
options: (a) Cash flows from financing activities and operating activities respectively
(b) Cash flows from investing activities and operating activities respectively
(c) Cash flows from financing activity and investing activity respectively
(d) There is an option to present both as cash flows from operating activities
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (c) Cash flows from financing activity and investing activity respectively

question: Cash flow is based upon: Answer:
options: (a) Accrual basis of accounting
(b) Cash basis of accounting
(c) Hybrid basis of accounting
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (b) Cash basis of accounting

question: An entity shall report Answer:
options: (a) Separately major classes of net cash receipts or net cash payments as the case may be arising from investing and financing activities
(b) Separately major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments arising from investing and financing activities
(c) Collectively major classes of net cash receipts or net cash payments as the case may be arising from investing and financing activities
(d) Collectively major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments arising from investing and financing activities
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (b) Separately major classes of gross cash receipts and gross cash payments arising from investing and financing activities

question: An entity has bank balance in foreign currency aggregating to USD 100 (equivalent to ₹ 4,500) at the beginning of the year. Presuming no other transaction taking place, the entity reported a profit before tax of ₹ 100 on account of exchange gain on the bank balance in foreign currency at the end of the year. What would be the closing cash and cash equivalents as per the balance sheet? Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 4,500

question: Under Ind AS 7 Statement of Cash Flows, cash flows arising from the following operating, investing or financing activities may be reported on a net basis: Answer:
options: (a) Cash receipts and payments on behalf of customers when the cash flows reflect the activities of the customer rather than those of the entity
(b) Entity has a legally enforceable right to set off the recognised amounts
(c) Entity intents to either settle the net cash outflows on a net basis or to realise the cash inflows and settle the liabilities simultaneously
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (a) Cash receipts and payments on behalf of customers when the cash flows reflect the activities of the customer rather than those of the entity

question: During the financial year 20X1-20X2, ABC Limited have paid various taxes & reproduced the below mentioned records for your perusal: - Capital gain tax of ₹ 2 crore on sale of office premises at a sale consideration of ₹ 100 crore. - Income Tax of ₹ 3 crore on Business profits amounting ₹ 30 crore (assume entire business profit as cash profit). - Dividend Distribution Tax of ₹ 1 crore on payment of dividend amounting ₹ 10 crore to its shareholders. - Income tax Refund of ₹ 2 crore (Refund on taxes paid in earlier periods for business profits) Calculate cashflow from investing activities. Answer:
options: (a) ₹ 29 crore
(b) ₹ 32 crore
(c) ₹ 98 crore
(d) (₹ 11 crore)
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (c) ₹ 98 crore

question: Cash flows from operations will increase due to: Answer:
options: (a) Increase in current assets
(b) Decrease in current liabilities
(c) Neither of two
(d) Both (a) and (b) above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (c) Neither of two

question: Which of the following is incorrect? Answer:
options: (a) Equity investments are excluded from cash equivalents unless they are, in substance, cash equivalents, for example in the case of preference shares acquired within a short period of their maturity and with a specified redemption date
(b) Bank borrowings are generally considered to be investing activities
(c) Where bank overdrafts which are repayable on demand form an integral part of an entity's cash management, bank overdrafts are included as a component of cash and cash equivalents.
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (b) Bank borrowings are generally considered to be investing activities

question: Which of the following is not a characteristic of an entitys cash equivalents, as defined by Ind AS 7? Answer:
options: (a) A short-term investment
(b) A highly liquid investment
(c) An investment which is readily convertible into known amounts of cash
(d) An investment which is subject to significant risk of changes in value
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (d) An investment which is subject to significant risk of changes in value

question: Under indirect cash flow method Answer:
options: (a) Profit or loss is adjusted for the effects of transactions of a cash nature, any deferrals or accruals of past or future operating cash receipts or payments
(b) Statement of changes in net assets/equity is adjusted for the effects of transactions of a cash nature, any deferrals or accruals of past or future operating cash receipts or payments
(c) Profit or loss is adjusted for the effects of transactions of a non-cash nature, any deferrals or accruals of past or future operating cash receipts or payments
(d) Statement of changes in net assets/equity is adjusted for the effects of transactions of a non-cash nature, any deferrals or accruals of past or future operating cash receipts or payments
explanation: [CHAPTER 3 - Ind AS on Presentation of Items in the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 7 “Statement of Cash Flows”] Correct Option: (d) Statement of changes in net assets/equity is adjusted for the effects of transactions of a non-cash nature, any deferrals or accruals of past or future operating cash receipts or payments

question: The selection and application of accounting policies for similar transactions, other events and conditions shall be: Answer:
options: (a) Consistent always
(b) Consistent unless an Ind AS specifically requires or permits categorisation of items for which different policies may be appropriate
(c) Consistent only if Ind AS specifically requires or permits categorisation of items for which different policies are not appropriate
(d) Consistent unless the policy is not favourable to the entity
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (a) Consistent always

question: Which of the following is treated as a change in the accounting policies in accordance with Ind AS 8, Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting Estimates and Errors? Answer:
options: (a) Change in composition of reportable segments
(b) Changes in functional currency
(c) Change in classification of financial assets
(d) Changes in measurement method of Inventory
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (d) Changes in measurement method of Inventory

question: Which of the following shall be considered as a change in accounting policy? Answer:
options: (a) the application of an accounting policy for transactions, other events or conditions that differ in substance from those previously occurring; and
(b) the application of a new accounting policy for transactions, other events or conditions that occurred previously or material
(c) Both of the above
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (b) the application of a new accounting policy for transactions, other events or conditions that occurred previously or material

question: Which of the following items are examples of changes in accounting estimates? (i) A loss allowance for expected credit losses, applying Ind AS 109, Financial Instruments; (ii) The net realisable value of an item of inventory, applying Ind AS 2 Inventories; (iii) The depreciation expense for an item of property, plant and equipment, applying Ind AS 16; and (iv) A provision for warranty obligations, applying Ind AS 37, Provisions, Contingent Liabilities and Contingent Assets. Answer:
options: (a) (i), (ii), (iii)
(c) (i), (ii), (iii), (iv)
(d) (ii), (iii)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (c) (i), (ii), (iii), (iv)

question: According to Ind AS 8, when a change in accounting policy is applied retrospectively, the entity shall adjust: (i) Opening balance of each affected component of equity for the earliest prior period presented. (ii) Other comparative amounts disclosed for earliest prior period presented. (iii) Other comparative amounts disclosed for each prior period presented. (iv) Opening balance of each affected component of equity for each prior period presented. State which of the above statements are correct. Answer:
options: (a) (i) and (ii)
(b) (i) and (iii)
(c) (ii) and (iv)
(d) (iii) and (iv)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (b) (i) and (iii)

question: Some new standards and amendments have been issued in the month of March 20X2, but it was effective from 1st April 20X2. In accordance with Ind AS 8, what is the provision in this regard when the entity has not applied a new Ind AS that has been issued but is not yet effective? Answer:
options: (a) Treated as change in accounting policy in the subsequent year
(b) Only disclosure of the facts is required

(c) Disclose both this fact and any known or reasonably estimable information relevant to assessing the possible impact that application of the new Ind AS will have on the entitys financial statements in the period of initial application

(d) Disclose both this fact and any known or reasonably estimable information relevant to assessing the possible impact that application of the new Ind AS will have on the entitys financial statements in the current period
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (c) Disclose both this fact and any known or reasonably estimable information relevant to assessing the possible impact that application of the new Ind AS will have on the entitys financial statements in the period of initial application

question: According to Ind AS 8, prior period errors shall be corrected: Answer:
options: (a) Prospectively
(b) Retrospectively
(c) Entity has a choice to correct prospectively or retrospectively
(d) Prospectively and disclosure are required
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (b) Retrospectively

question: In some cases, it is difficult to distinguish between a change of estimate and a change in accounting policy. How should the entity treat the same? Answer:
options: (a) Entire change as a change in accounting policy
(b) Entire change as a change in accounting estimate with appropriate disclosure
(c) Apportion, on a reasonable basis, between the change in estimate and the change in accounting policy and treat accordingly. Consistency should be there in all the future periods
(d) Ignore the transaction
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (b) Entire change as a change in accounting estimate with appropriate disclosure

question: A company made some changes in accounting policies and accounted for them in financial year 20X1 20X2. Due to changes in accounting policies, retrospective adjustment has tax effect related to previous years along with effect on the transaction. How will this be accounted for and disclosed? Answer:
options: (a) In accordance with Ind AS 8
(b) In accordance with Ind AS 12
(c) Tax effect in accordance with Ind AS 12 and transaction effect in accordance with Ind AS 8
(d) Entity has the choice between options (a) and (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (c) Tax effect in accordance with Ind AS 12 and transaction effect in accordance with Ind AS 8

question: Applying a new accounting policy to transactions, other events and conditions as if that policy had always been applied is considered as __________ Answer:
options: (a) Correction of error
(b) Retrospective application
(c) Retrospective restatement
(d) Prospective application
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 1: Ind AS 8 “Accounting Policies, Changes in Accounting] Correct Option: (b) Retrospective application

question: The objective of Ind AS 10 is to prescribe: Answer:
options: (a) The disclosures that an entity should give about the date when the financial statements were approved for issue
(b) The disclosures about events after the reporting period
(c) None of the above
(d) Both (a) and (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (d) Both (a) and (b)

question: What is the date of approval for issue of the financial statements prepared for the reporting period from 1st April, 20X1 to 31st March, 20X2, in a situation where following dates are available? Answer:
options: (a) Completion of preparation of financial statements 15th April, 20X2
(b) Board reviews and approves for issue 25th April, 20X2
(c) Available to shareholders 16th May, 20X2
(d) Filed with regulatory authority 30th May, 20X2
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (b) Board reviews and approves for issue 25th April, 20X2

question: On 15th April, 20X2, a major earthquake disrupted the entire operations of a reputed company. The Company suffered huge loss due to the damage caused to its factories and other business premises. The Companys insurance policy does not cover the risk of loss arising from natural disasters. The Company does not have sufficient internal funds or the availability of external finance to rebuild the infrastructure necessary for it to resume its business operations. The Board of the company is also not sure about the future of the company. The Company has prepared the financial statements for the year ending 31st March, 20X2 which is approved in the board meeting dated 20th April, 20X2. How this event impact the financial statement of the company? Answer:
options: (a) Adjustment in financials are required
(b) Disclosure is required
(c) Nothing is required
(d) On the discretion of the management
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (a) Adjustment in financials are required

question: According to Ind AS 10, when management of an entity is required to issue its financial statements to a supervisory board for issue, the financial statements are said to be approved when: Answer:
options: (a) Shareholders approve the financial statements
(b) Filed with the regulatory authorities
(c) Approved by the supervisory Board
(d) Management approve the financial statements for issue to the supervisory Board
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (d) Management approve the financial statements for issue to the supervisory Board

question: A company XYZ took a long-term loan from bank. Before the end of the reporting date there is a breach in the terms which are material for this loan. The amount stands payable on demand by the company to bank. After the reporting date but before approval of the financial statements for issue, company entered into an agreement with the bank, pursuant to which the loan is not payable on demand. This loan will be treated as: Answer:
options: (a) Adjusting event
(b) Non-adjusting event
(c) Principal amount is non-adjusting event and interest portion is adjusting event
(d) The company has the choice to treat it either adjusting event or non-adjusting event
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (a) Adjusting event

question: The management of a company decided and announced a plan to discontinue the operations and liquidate the company after the reporting date. According to Ind AS 10 Events after the reporting period the company shall: Answer:
options: (a) Prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis
(b) Not prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis
(c) Prepare the financial statement on a going concern basis with disclosures as per Ind AS 1
(d) Prepare the financial statement on a going concern basis with no disclosures requirement
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (b) Not prepare its financial statements on a going concern basis

question: Moon Ltd having issued share capital of 15,00,000 shares decided to offer two options for dividend per share- Option (i)- 10 Bottles of perfume (Fair Market Value (FMV) per bottle= ₹ 75) Option (ii)- Dividend payment of ₹ 700 The probability of shareholders selecting non-cash vis--vis cash option is estimated at 60:40. Calculate the amount at which dividend shall be initially recognised. Later on, if on date of settlement the FMV of bottle is ₹ 90 and accordingly, the ratio for non-cash vis--vis cash option becomes 80:20, then how much amount shall be debited to equity? Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (c) ₹ 1,09,50,00,000, ₹ 19,50,00,000

question: Event after the reporting period are those events that occur between the end of the reporting period and the date ...................... Answer:
options: (a) When the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors
(b) Of Annual General Meeting
(c) Of signing of the financial statements by the auditors
(d) Of finalization of the financial statements by the management after final discussion with auditors
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (a) When the financial statements are approved by the Board of Directors

question: On 15th January, 20X2, Alpha Ltd. filed a suit against Beta Ltd. for recovery of ₹ 10 lakhs. On 15th April, 20X2, the court case confirms that Beta Ltd. will have to pay the amount to Alpha Ltd. The financial statements are approved by the Board on 20th May, 20X2. What will be the treatment of ₹ 10 lakhs in the financial statements of Beta Ltd. on the reporting date i.e. 31st March, 20X2 as per Ind AS 10? Answer:
options: (a) Disclose it as a contingent liability
(b) Recognise liability for ₹ 10 lakhs
(c) Recognise provision for ₹ 10 lakhs
(d) No treatment
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (c) Recognise provision for ₹ 10 lakhs

question: The financial statements of Star Ltd. for financial year 20X1-20X2 were approved by the Board for issue on 24th May, 20X2. The management discovered a major fraud and decided to reopen the books of account. The financial statements were subsequently approved by the Board of Directors on 31st May, 20X2. What is the date of approval for issue as per Ind AS 10 in the given case? Answer:
options: (a) 24th May, 20X2
(b) 31st May, 20X2
(c) Either (a) or (b)
(d) Neither (a) nor (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 2: Ind AS 10 “Events after the Reporting Period”] Correct Option: (b) 31st May, 20X2

question: Characteristics of the asset or liability are considered if market participants would take those characteristics into account when pricing the asset or liability at the measurement date. Such characteristics include: Answer:
options: (a) condition of the asset
(b) location of the asset
(c) restrictions on the sale or use of the asset
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: The asset or liability measured at fair value shall be: Answer:
options: (a) a standalone asset or liability
(b) a group of assets, a group of liabilities or a group of assets and liabilities
(c) Either of (a) and (b)
(d) Neither of (a) and (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (c) Either of (a) and (b)

question: Revisions resulting from a change in the valuation technique or its application shall be accounted for as Answer:
options: (a) Change in accounting policy as per Ind AS 8
(b) Change in accounting estimate as per Ind AS 8
(c) Change in valuation technique is not permitted
(d) Prior period error as per Ind AS 8
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (b) Change in accounting estimate as per Ind AS 8

question: The market that maximises the amount that would be received to sell the asset or minimises the amount that would be paid to transfer the liability, after taking into account transaction costs and transport costs is called ___________ Answer:
options: (a) Principal market
(b) Most advantageous market
(c) Primary market
(d) Active market
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (b) Most advantageous market

question: The basic rule related to inputs to valuation techniques as per Ind AS 113 are Answer:
options: (a) maximising the use of relevant observable and unobservable inputs
(b) minimising the use of relevant observable and unobservable inputs
(c) maximising the use of relevant observable inputs and minimising the use of unobservable inputs
(d) minimising the use of relevant observable inputs and maximising the use of unobservable inputs
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (c) maximising the use of relevant observable inputs and minimising the use of unobservable inputs

question: The measurement requirements of Ind AS 113 applies to Answer:
options: (a) share based payment transactions within the scope of IFRS 2 Share?based Payment
(b) leasing transactions accounted for in accordance with IFRS 16 Leases
(c) Assets for which recoverable amount is fair value less costs of disposals in accordance with Ind AS 36
(d) measurements of net realisable value in IAS 2 Inventories or value in use in IAS 36 Impairment of Assets
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (c) Assets for which recoverable amount is fair value less costs of disposals in accordance with Ind AS 36

question: The highest and best use of a non? financial asset while measuring the fair value takes into account the use of the asset that is Answer:
options: (a) physically possible
(b) legally permissible
(c) financially feasible
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: A fair value measurement assumes that the transaction to sell the asset or transfer the liability takes place either: Answer:
options: (a) in the principal market or in the most advantageous market
(b) in the principal market or in the primary market
(c) in the primary market or in the secondary market
(d) in the primary market or in the most advantageous market
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (a) in the principal market or in the most advantageous market

question: The price paid to acquire the asset or received to assume the liability is called Answer:
options: (a) transaction price (an entry price)
(b) transaction price (an exit price)
(c) Settlement price (an entry price)
(d) Settlement price (an exit price)
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (a) transaction price (an entry price)

question: As per Ind AS 113, which of the followings is not a widely used valuation technique? Answer:
options: (a) Net present value approach
(b) Cost approach
(c) Income approach
(d) Market approach
explanation: [CHAPTER 4 - Ind AS on Measurement based on Accounting Policies | Unit 3: Ind AS 113 “Fair Value Measurement”] Correct Option: (a) Net present value approach

question: Which of the following criteria is not correct in case of identification of contract with the customer to be accounted for under Ind AS 115? Answer:
options: (a) the parties to the contract have approved the contract in writing only
(b) the entity can identify each partys rights regarding the goods or services to be transferred
(c) the entity can identify the payment terms for the goods or services to be transferred
(d) the contract has commercial substance
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (a) the parties to the contract have approved the contract in writing only

question: As per Ind AS 115, an entity shall combine two or more contracts entered into at or near the same time with the same customer and account for the contracts as a single contract when Answer:
options: (a) the contracts are negotiated as a package with a single commercial objective
(b) the amount of consideration to be paid in one contract depends on the price or performance of the other contract
(c) the goods or services promised in the contracts are a single performance obligation
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: An entity shall account for a contract modification as a separate contract when Answer:
options: (a) the scope of the contract increases because of the addition of promised goods or services that are distinct
(b) the price of the contract increases by an amount of consideration that reflects the entitys stand-alone selling prices of the additional promised goods or services
(c) Either (a) or (b)
(d) Both (a) or (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (d) Both (a) or (b)

question: Impairment loss as per Ind AS 115 shall be recognised in Answer:
options: (a) Other Comprehensive Income
(b) Profit or Loss
(c) Contract Assets
(d) Other Reserves
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (b) Profit or Loss

question: Ind AS 115 applies to Answer:
options: (a) Lease contracts within the scope of Ind AS 116 Leases
(b) Financial instruments and other contractual rights or obligations within the scope of Ind AS 109, Ind AS 110, Ind AS 111, Ind AS 27 and Ind AS 28
(c) Non-monetary exchanges between entities in the same line of business to facilitate sales to customers or potential customers
(d) Non-monetary exchanges between entities in different line of business to facilitate sales to customers or potential customers
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (d) Non-monetary exchanges between entities in different line of business to facilitate sales to customers or potential customers

question: _________ is the amount of consideration to which an entity expects to be entitled in exchange for transferring promised goods or services to a customer, excluding amounts collected on behalf of third parties Answer:
options: (a) Transaction price
(b) Market price
(c) Ordinary price
(d) Fair price
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (a) Transaction price

question: Where the penalty is inherent in determination of transaction price of a contract, it shall form part of Answer:
options: (a) Fixed consideration
(b) Variable consideration
(c) Non-cash consideration
(d) Not included in consideration
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (b) Variable consideration

question: Which of the following cost shall be recognises as an asset while obtaining a contract with a customer if the entity expects to recover those costs Answer:
options: (a) Sales commission
(b) General and administrative costs
(c) Costs of wasted materials, labour or other resources
(d) Costs that relate to past performance
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (a) Sales commission

question: An entity has entered into a contract with a customer which does not meet the criteria for identifying the contract and the entity has received consideration from the customer. In such a case the entity shall recognise the consideration as revenue only when Answer:
options: (a) the entity has no remaining obligations to transfer goods or services to the customer and consideration promised by the customer has been received by the entity and is non-refundable
(b) the contract has been terminated and the consideration received from the customer is non-refundable

(c) the entity has no remaining obligations to transfer goods or services to the customer and all, or substantially all, of the consideration promised by the customer has been received by the entity and is refundable
(d) Either (a) or (b) Chapter 5 Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers 23
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (d) Either (a) or (b) Chapter 5 Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers 23

question: To determine the transaction price for contracts in which a customer promises consideration in a form other than cash, an entity shall measure the non-cash consideration at
options: (a) Actual price
(b) Transaction price
(c) Fair value
(d) Market price
explanation: [CHAPTER 5 - Ind AS 115 “Revenue from Contracts with Customers] Correct Option: (c) Fair value

question: Hari Limited is a manufacturer of Carton Boxes. The cost of the stock as on 31.12.20X1 was ₹ 50 per box. The accountant noted that the subsequent sale was made on 31.1.20X2 at ₹ 40 per box. The accountant also noted that there were subsequent expenses for some rectification on the entire physical stock that was available as at year end at the rate of ₹ 15 per box to saleable condition. The company seeks your opinion as to the amount of net realisable value and written down loss for the closing stock as per Ind AS 2. Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 25 and ₹ 25

question: At the end of an accounting period, the cost of a company's inventory is ₹ 4,50,000. This includes damaged items with a cost of ₹ 25,000 which are expected to be sold for only ₹ 10,000 (less selling expenses of 5%). All other items of inventory have a net realisable value which exceeds cost. As per Ind AS 2, the amount at which the company's inventory should be recognized at the end of the period is: Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (c) ₹ 4,34,500

question: W Limited, a company manufactures and sells towels and bedsheets using cotton, yarn, dyes and chemicals. W limited also sells cotton and intermediator product yarn occasionally in exceptional cases. Which of the following items are to be classified as inventories in books of accounts of W limited: Answer:
options: (a) Cotton, yarn, towel, bedsheets, dyes and Chemicals
(b) Towel and Bedsheets only
(c) Cotton, Yarn, Dyes and Chemicals only
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (a) Cotton, yarn, towel, bedsheets, dyes and Chemicals

question: Which of the following inventory would be measured at lower of cost and net realisable value? Answer:
options: (a) Sand
(b) Barite
(c) Plastic
(d) Limestone
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (c) Plastic

question: Normal Annual Capacity of the Plant X is 1,000 Units. During the year ended 31st March 20X2, the company is able to produce only 700 units (due to sudden strike of union labour). During the current year, company have incurred ₹ 21,000 of fixed over heads. Inventory Quantity as at 31.3.20X2 is 200 Units. Determine the amount of fixed overheads allocation that needs to be done on the inventory lying in hand as at 31.3.20X2 as per Ind AS 2? Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (c) ₹ 4,200

question: P Ltd. has a plant with the normal capacity to produce 5,00,000 units of a product per annum and the expected fixed overhead is ₹ 15,00,000. However, actual production is 3,75,000 units. Amount of fixed overhead to be included in the cost of inventory would be Answer:
options: (d) Nil
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 11,25,000

question: A Ltd shipped inventory on consignment to B Ltd. How should the consigned inventory to be treated assuming the inventory is unsold by B Ltd.? Answer:
options: (a) To be measured as Inventory in A Ltd book
(b) To be measured as Inventory in B Ltd book
(c) To be recognized as revenue in A Ltd
(d) To be recognized as liability in B Ltd
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (a) To be measured as Inventory in A Ltd book

question: V Ltd. purchases cars from several countries and sells them to Asian countries. V Ltd. incurred many expenses during the period on such cars from their purchase to sale. Which of the following cost is allowed for inclusion in the cost of inventory? Answer:
options: (a) ₹ 20,00,000 as Salaries of accounting department
(b) ₹ 15,00,000 of Sales commission paid to sales agents
(c) ₹ 30,00,000 as after sales warranty costs
(d) ₹ 10,00,000 as Insurance of purchases
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 1: Ind AS 2 “Inventories”] Correct Option: (d) ₹ 10,00,000 as Insurance of purchases

question: Progress Ltd chooses to revalue property under Ind AS 16. On 31st March 20X1, their head office building is valued at ₹ 30 lakh when it is recorded in the financial statements at historical cost of ₹ 25 lakh with ₹ 4.5 lakh of accumulated depreciation charged against it. Which of the following statements is true regarding the accounting treatment of the property? Answer:
options: (a) A revaluation gain of ₹ 5 lakh should be recorded through other comprehensive income, grouped with other items that will not subsequently be reclassified to profit or loss
(b) A revaluation gain of ₹ 5 lakh should be recorded through profit or loss
(c) A revaluation gain of ₹ 9.5 lakh should be recorded through other comprehensive income, grouped with other items that will not subsequently be reclassified to profit or loss
(d) A revaluation gain of ₹ 9.5 lakh should be recorded through other comprehensive income, grouped with other items that will subsequently be reclassified to profit or loss
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (c) A revaluation gain of ₹ 9.5 lakh should be recorded through other comprehensive income, grouped with other items that will not subsequently be reclassified to profit or loss

question: Under Ind AS 16, which two subsequent accounting treatments are allowed subsequently to initial recognition? Answer:
options: (a) Cost model and present value model
(b) Cost model and revaluation model
(c) Fair value model and revaluation model
(d) Fair value model and cost model
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (b) Cost model and revaluation model

question: When it is _____that future economic benefits associated with an asset will flow to the entity, and the cost of the asset can be _____ measured, it should be recognized as an asset. Answer:
options: (a) Possible, reasonably
(b) Possible, reliably
(c) Probable, reliably
(d) Probable, reasonably
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (c) Probable, reliably

question: Which of these is an allowable cost of an asset for capitalisation under Ind AS 16? Answer:
options: (a) Professional fees
(b) General overheads
(c) Initial operating losses
(d) Administration expenses
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (a) Professional fees

question: Under Ind AS 16, how often should the useful life of an asset be reviewed? Answer:
options: (a) At least at each financial year end
(b) Every six months
(c) At managements discretion
(d) Never
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (a) At least at each financial year end

question: When an asset is sold or disposed of, where is the gain or loss recognized? Answer:
options: (a) Asset disposal account
(b) Profit and loss
(c) Revaluation reserve
(d) Depreciation
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (b) Profit and loss

question: A Limited has stopped manufacturing operations in its plant for 3 months in the year ended 31st March, 20X1. How should A limited account for depreciation relating to the 3 months in which plant was idle under Ind AS 16? Answer:
options: (a) No depreciation should be charged for 3 months
(b) Depreciation for 3 months in which plant was idle should be recognized in other comprehensive income
(c) Depreciation for 3 months in which plant was idle should be recognized in retained earnings
(d) Depreciation for 3 months in which plant was idle should be recognized in profit or loss
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (d) Depreciation for 3 months in which plant was idle should be recognized in profit or loss

question: If one large asset has a number of individual components with different useful lives, how should this be depreciated? Answer:
options: (a) Treat as one asset and depreciate in accordance with highest useful life of the component
(b) Break down into different components and depreciate every component separately as per the useful life of that component
(c) Expense it all
(d) Treat as one asset, but disclose only in the notes to the financial statements
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (b) Break down into different components and depreciate every component separately as per the useful life of that component

question: India Turnings Limited has adopted revaluation model, as per Ind AS, since 1st April, 20X1 to measure its property, plant and equipment (PPE) and have revalued it as follows: (i) As on 1st April, 20X1 PPE has been revalued up by ₹ 3,00,000. (ii) As on 31st March, 20X2 PPE has been revalued down by ₹ 3,60,000 (iii) As on 31st March, 20X3 PPE has been revalued up by ₹ 5,00,000 How will the increase in year 20X2-20X3 be recognized in the financials of India Turnings Limited? Answer:
options: (a) ₹ 5,00,000 is credited to other comprehensive income
(b) ₹ 60,000 is credited to profit and loss account and ₹ 4,40,000 is credited to other comprehensive income
(c) ₹ 60,000 is credited to other comprehensive income and ₹ 4,40,000 is credited to profit and loss account
(d) ₹ 5,00,000 is credited to profit and loss account
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 60,000 is credited to profit and loss account and ₹ 4,40,000 is credited to other comprehensive income

question: When the revaluation model is used for PPE the gain on revaluation should be treated as Answer:
options: (a) Income in the Statement of profit and loss for the period
(b) Gain from revaluation in the income statement
(c) A revaluation surplus accounted in OCI
(d) An extraordinary gain or loss in the income statement
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 2: Ind AS 16 “Property, Plant and Equipment”] Correct Option: (c) A revaluation surplus accounted in OCI

question: Borrowing costs do not include Answer:
options: (a) Interest expense calculated using the effective interest rate method as described in Ind AS 109 Financial Instruments
(b) Interest in respect of lease liabilities recognized in accordance with Ind AS 116, Leases
(c) Exchange differences arising from foreign currency borrowings to the extent that they are regarded as an adjustment to interest costs
(d) Interest expenses on own finance resources or interest notional expenses
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (d) Interest expenses on own finance resources or interest notional expenses

question: In determining the borrowing costs to be capitalised, the amount of expenditure on a qualifying asset include only those expenditures that have resulted in Answer:
options: (a) Payments of cash
(b) Transfers of other assets
(c) The assumption of interest-bearing liabilities
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: In determining the borrowing costs to be capitalised, the amount of expenditure on a qualifying asset are not reduced by Answer:
options: (a) Progress payments received
(b) Grants received in connection with the asset
(c) Income on temporary investment of specific borrowings
(d) Both (a) and (b)
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (c) Income on temporary investment of specific borrowings

question: Which of the following would be considered as borrowing cost to be capitalised? Answer:
options: (a) Interest on working capital
(b) Interest on borrowings used for manufacturing inventories in large quantities on a repetitive basis
(c) Interest on borrowings utilised to acquire biological assets measured at fair value
(d) Dividend paid on redeemable preference shares used to fund the development of a qualifying asset
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (d) Dividend paid on redeemable preference shares used to fund the development of a qualifying asset

question: What will be the treatment of exchange difference resulting into unrealised gain while capitalising the borrowing cost on foreign currency borrowings taken for construction of a qualifying asset? Answer:
options: (a) It would not be adjusted to interest even if there was an adjustment to interest in the previous year on account of unrealised exchange loss on settlement or translation of same borrowings
(b) It would be adjusted to interest to the extent of an adjustment to interest in the previous year on account of unrealised exchange loss on settlement or translation of same borrowings

(c) It will be adjusted to interest irrespective of the fact that whether there was an adjustment to interest in the previous year on account of unrealised exchange loss (on settlement or translation of same borrowings) or not
(d) It will be adjusted to interest fully only if there was an adjustment to interest in the previous year on account of unrealised exchange loss on settlement or translation of same borrowings
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (b) It would be adjusted to interest to the extent of an adjustment to interest in the previous year on account of unrealised exchange loss on settlement or translation of same borrowings

question: Which of the following is not a qualifying asset? Answer:
options: (a) Financial assets
(b) Investment properties
(c) Intangible plants
(d) Bearer plants
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (a) Financial assets

question: Adit Labs are planning to expand their business and open two more branches in the vicinity of two new hospitals being built in the area. The enterprise is using funds from their general borrowings for this expansion project. The finance director of the company has briefly read about the capitalisation of the interest paid on the borrowings. He has sought your clarification on this matter if his entity can capitalise interest of 10% which is the highest interest rate of all the borrowings they have made during the year. Which of the following are correct about the capitalisation of interest on borrowings made by a company as per Ind AS 23 Borrowing Costs? Answer:
options: (a) Finance director is right, and he can use 10% as capitalisation rate for calculating the eligible borrowing costs to be capitalised on the qualifying asset

(b) Capitalisation rate should be weighted average of all the borrowing costs applicable to the borrowings of the enterprise that are outstanding during the period, other than borrowings made specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset

(c) Interest paid on general borrowing have to be calculated in accordance with ICDS (Income Computation and Disclosure Standards) which is also required for calculation of current tax and deferred tax
(d) Entity should use the lowest interest rate of all the borrowings outstanding during the period as capitalisation rate to calculate the eligible borrowing costs
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (b) Capitalisation rate should be weighted average of all the borrowing costs applicable to the borrowings of the enterprise that are outstanding during the period, other than borrowings made specifically for the purpose of obtaining a qualifying asset

question: The capitalisation rate is Answer:
options: (a) The weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to all the general borrowings of the entity that are outstanding during the period
(b) The weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to all the general and specific borrowings of the entity that are outstanding during the period
(c) The weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to all the specific borrowings of the entity that are outstanding during the period
(d) The weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to those general borrowings of the entity only that are used during the period for construction of that particular qualifying asset
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 3: Ind AS 23 “Borrowing Costs”] Correct Option: (a) The weighted average of the borrowing costs applicable to all the general borrowings of the entity that are outstanding during the period

question: Recoverable amount of an asset or cash generating unit is ____________. Answer:
options: (a) Higher of Fair value less costs of disposal and Value in use
(b) Lower of net realisable value and cost
(c) Higher of fair value and value in use
(d) Higher of market value less costs of disposal and value in use
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (a) Higher of Fair value less costs of disposal and Value in use

question: Which of the following is not covered by Ind AS 36, Impairment of Assets? Answer:
options: (a) Deferred tax assets
(b) Inventory
(c) Financial assets
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: When a cash-generating unit has an impairment loss, the loss must be firstly applied to_________. Answer:
options: (a) Asset with obvious impairment
(b) Goodwill
(c) Other assets of CGU on a pro-rata basis
(d) Based on management discretion
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (b) Goodwill

question: In case of estimation of cash flows for calculating value in use, future cash flows are estimated in the currency in which they will be generated and then discounted using a discount rate appropriate for that currency. An entity translates the present value using the ____________ at the date of the value in use calculation. Answer:
options: (a) Closing rate
(b) Spot exchange rate
(c) Average rate
(d) Incremental borrowing rate
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (b) Spot exchange rate

question: In measuring value in use, cash flow projections should be based on the budgets/forecasts covering a maximum period of _______________, unless a longer period can be justified. Answer:
options: (a) Three years
(b) Five years
(c) Ten years
(d) Life of asset which is subject to impairment assessment
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (b) Five years

question: When an impairment loss occurs, the carrying amount of the asset should be reduced to its __________. Answer:
options: (a) Fair Value
(b) Recoverable amount
(c) Fair Value less cost to disposal
(d) Value in use
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (b) Recoverable amount

question: Smallest identifiable group of assets that generates cash inflows that are largely independent of the cash inflows from other assets or groups of assets is known as ________ Answer:
options: (a) Cash-generating unit
(b) Branch
(c) Department
(d) Operating Segment
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (a) Cash-generating unit

question: __________ is considered as recoverable amount when it is not possible to measure the fair value less costs of disposal for an asset. Answer:
options: (a) Market value
(b) Replacement value
(c) Value in use
(d) Carrying amount
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (c) Value in use

question: Which of the following is not an internal indication of impairment? Answer:
options: (a) Economic performance of the asset is worse than expected
(b) Physical damage of the asset
(c) Decline in market value
(d) Asset is part of a plans to discontinue or restructure the operation
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (c) Decline in market value

question: Which of the following is required to be tested for impairment annually irrespective of the presence of indications of impairment or not? Answer:
options: (a) Intangible asset with an indefinite useful life
(b) Intangible asset not yet available for use
(c) Goodwill acquired in a business combination
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 4: Ind AS 36 “Impairment of Assets”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: A newly set up dot-com entity has recently completed one of its highly publicized research and development projects. It seeks your advice on the accuracy of the following statements made by one of its stakeholders. State which one is true? Answer:
options: (a) Costs incurred during the research phase can be capitalized
(b) Costs incurred during the development phase can be capitalized if criteria such as technical feasibility of the project being established are met
(c) Training costs of technicians used in research can be capitalized
(d) Designing of jigs and tools qualify as research activities
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (b) Costs incurred during the development phase can be capitalized if criteria such as technical feasibility of the project being established are met

question: With respect to valuation of goodwill and recognition of the same on acquisition of another entity. Ind AS 38 Intangibles assets establishes general principles for the recognition and measurement of intangible assets in the financial statements. The standard requires any entity to recognize the intangible assets in the financial statements if and only if: i) it is probable that the future economic benefits which are attributable to the asset will flow to the enterprise; and ii) the cost of the asset can be reliably measured Which of the following is NOT correct about the intangible assets? Answer:
options: (a) The above recognition criteria are applicable to both the costs incurred to acquire intangible assets and those generated internally
(b) Internally generated goodwill is prohibited to be recognized by the standard. Only acquired goodwill can be recognized as an intangible asset in the financial statements
(c) In case of brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and similar intangible assets can be recognized both when generated internally as well as acquired separately
(d) In case of research and development phase of an internally generated assets, standard permits capitalisation only in the development phase
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (c) In case of brands, mastheads, publishing titles, and similar intangible assets can be recognized both when generated internally as well as acquired separately

question: Amortisation of an intangible asset ceases _________. Answer:
options: (a) when the asset is derecognized
(b) when the asset is withdrawn from use
(c) at the earlier when the asset is classified as held for sale or when the asset is derecognized
(d) at the later of asset is classified as held for sale or derecognized
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (c) at the earlier when the asset is classified as held for sale or when the asset is derecognized

question: AG Limited is developing a new production process. During 20X1-20X2, expenditure incurred was ₹ 11 lakhs of which ₹ 8 lakhs was incurred before 1st January, 20X2 and ₹ 3 lakhs was incurred between January and March 20X2. The company is able to demonstrate that on 1st January, 20X2, the production process met the criteria for recognition as an intangible asset. The recoverable amount of the know-how embodied in the process (including future cash outflows to complete the process before it is available for use) is estimated to be ₹ 2 lakhs as at 31st March, 20X2. What is the carrying value of intangible asset at the end of the year? Answer:
options: (a) ₹ 11 lakhs
(b) ₹ 8 lakhs
(c) ₹ 2 lakhs
(d) ₹ 3 lakhs
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (c) ₹ 2 lakhs

question: AG Limited has purchased a computer with various additional software. These are integral part of the computer. Which of the following are true in the context of Ind AS 38? Answer:
options: (a) Recognize Computer and software as tangible asset
(b) Recognize tangible and intangible separately
(c) Recognize computer and software as intangible asset
(d) None of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (a) Recognize Computer and software as tangible asset

question: Which of the following is not covered within the scope of Ind AS 38? Answer:
options: (a) Intangible assets held-for-sale in the ordinary course of business
(b) Assets arising from employee benefits
(c) Noncurrent Intangible assets held for sale
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: An intangible asset with a finite useful life should be amortised over Answer:
options: (a) Its expected useful life
(b) A period determined by management
(c) Five years
(d) No foreseeable limit
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (a) Its expected useful life

question: Which of the following is required to be tested for impairment annually irrespective of the presence of indications of impairment or not? Answer:
options: (a) Intangible asset with an indefinite useful life
(b) Intangible asset not yet available for use
(c) Goodwill acquired in a business combination
(d) All of the above
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (d) All of the above

question: AG Ltd acquired copyrights for ₹ 7,50,000 on 1st April 20X1. The Management assessed the copyrights useful life at 25 years from the date of acquisition. The entity will consume the copyrights future economic benefits evenly over 25 years from the date of acquisition. The fair value of the copyright at 31st March, 20X3 is ₹ 7,00,000. The entity shall measure the carrying amount of the copyright on 31st March, 20X3 at Answer:
explanation: [CHAPTER 6 - Ind AS on Assets of the Financial Statements | Unit 5: Ind AS 38 “Intangible Assets”] Correct Option: (b) ₹ 6,90,000

question: Which of the following items qualify as an intangible asset under Ind AS 38? Answer:
options: (a) Advertising and promotion on the launch of a huge product
